title: The five virtues as medicine
tomorrow: Bebe goes home Sunday. which thief is quieter in Simran now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, desire and respect: kaam turns a person into a thing, so see the soul. Now, the medicine.

Simran is at the kitchen table watching Bebe do her ankle exercises: heel up, heel down, the way the therapist's sheet on the fridge says, three times a day. Simran asks: so, five thieves, right? Lust, anger, greed, attachment, pride. Is there a medicine for each one, or do you just fight them forever? Bebe keeps lifting her heel. Bebe has done these every day since the boot came off, even the days she grumbled. She nods at the fridge and says: look.
screen: `HEEL UP, HEEL DOWN.` → `IS THERE A MEDICINE?` → `BEBE: LOOK AT THE FRIDGE.`

segments.voice: There is a medicine, and Sikh teachers name it in five virtues: sat, truth; santokh, contentment; daya, compassion; nimrata, humility; and pyaar, love. Teachers pair them with the thieves in different ways, but some pairings are plain: compassion against anger, contentment against greed, humility against pride. The idea runs straight back to Gurbani. In Asa di Var, on ang 466, the Guru says, in paraphrase: ego is a long illness, and its medicine is within it too. And on ang 62, Guru Nanak says truth is higher than everything, and higher still is truthful living. Living, not knowing. A virtue isn't a fact we learn about ourselves; it's something we do, on a Tuesday, when no one is checking. Here's what Bebe's fridge adds. A medicine isn't a speech; it's a dose. Small, daily, a little boring. Nobody heals an ankle by thinking hard about ankles, or by doing a month of exercises in one afternoon. You lift the heel today, and again tomorrow. So with the virtues: one honest sentence, one patient pause, one thing put back on the shelf. Here's the line to repeat tonight: the virtue is the dose, not the diagnosis. Simran takes a pen and writes under the therapy sheet: one virtue a day. Bebe reads it, puts on her glasses, reads it again, and says: good. You do yours, I'll do mine. Then she lifts her heel one more time than the sheet asks.
screen: `FIVE VIRTUES: TRUTH TO LOVE.` · `ANG 466: THE CURE IS WITHIN.` · `ANG 62: TRUTHFUL LIVING.` · `A DOSE, NOT A DIAGNOSIS.` · then, large: `THE MEDICINE.`

segments.voice: Choose one of the five: truth, contentment, compassion, humility or love. Picture one moment later today when you'll need it, and the small dose you could take: one honest sentence, one pause before answering, one thing left on the shelf. Hold that picture, and breathe.
The five virtues as medicine. Truth, contentment, compassion, humility and love, taken in small daily doses.
screen: `THE FIVE VIRTUES AS MEDICINE — today's word`.

segments.voice: The medicine: small doses, every day, like heel lifts on a sheet by the fridge. See you then.

howItsDone: Sikh teachers commonly set five virtues (sat, santokh, daya, nimrata, pyaar) against the five thieves, and Gurbani speaks of ego as an illness with a cure; the virtues are practiced in daily life, not only in prayer.

pairs: ego is an illness; the cure is within

myth: knowing the five virtues by name is most of the cure
ang 62: higher still is truthful living. the virtue is the dose, not the diagnosis.
Gurbani describes ego as an illness whose medicine is within it
the virtues work best as one big change, made all at once
like Bebe's heel lifts: small, daily, a little boring.

fork.setup: you've noticed you keep cutting people off in meetings. you've named the thief: pride. what fits today's idea of medicine?
options: a small daily dose: let one person finish first, each day.
a long, honest reflection on where your pride comes from.
a promise to stay silent in meetings from now on.
fork.reveal: the virtue is the dose, not the diagnosis: humility, taken small and daily, the way Bebe lifts her heel.

original.note: Gurmukhi: daaroo, medicine; on ang 466, ego is a long illness and its daaroo is within it.

trapdoor: what you thought: you beat the thieves by fighting them head on.
what it means: each thief has a medicine, a virtue taken in small daily doses.
what a scholar hears: haumai deeragh rog hai, daaroo bhee is maahi (ang 466), and sachahu orai sabh ko, upar sach aachaar (ang 62).

chat.says: ok five thieves, five medicines. can't i just pick the one i'm best at?
options: take a daily dose of the one you need most, like bebe's heel lifts.
sure. one virtue covers all five if you're really good at it.
the cure is knowing the list. once you can name them, you've won.
chat.meaning: The virtue is the dose, not the diagnosis: small, daily practice of the virtue the moment needs, as ang 62's truthful living.

Storyline (1681-1694): Bebe Jaswant twists her ankle in her chili garden (end of 1682), stays in Simran's room while she heals (1683), Simran drives her to physical therapy, snaps at her once and apologizes, and Bebe goes home on her own choice (1693); Bhua Kiran, Harjit's single sister, helps throughout; Maya and her grandmother Ruth (Christian) appear on 1681, 1686 and 1693. Simran's college acceptance (1689) is a side beat.
